[TritonToLinalg](fix) prioritize initialized argmin/max reductions (#3109)

The generic ReduceConverter can win over the existing ArgMin/ArgMax
patterns after #2440, leaving value/index accumulators uninitialized.
Give the specialized patterns a higher benefit while preserving their
matching rules and the generic fallback.

Derive integer value and index sentinels from each output's actual width
instead of fixed i8/u8 and i32 limits. Add MLIR coverage for pattern
priority, signed/unsigned identities, wide indices and generic fallback.

Signed-off-by: KanuaK <yihan_z@qq.com>
(cherry picked from commit b61482b2d4018039aeaa1668683e569392c02837)

[TritonToLinalg](fix) restore 950 slices with tail buffer reuse (#3007)

* [TritonToLinalg](perf) use direct select slices on Ascend 950

Avoid reconstructing zero-offset prefixes for contiguous Tail/Middle selects
on 950, where NPU IR supports unaligned UB copies. Keep the existing prefix
workaround on A2/A3 to avoid alignment-induced buffer expansion and retain
the dynamic-start bounds guard for both paths.

Add dual-target lowering checks and dynamic-offset correctness coverage for
boundary, empty-interval, dtype and loop-carried cases.

Signed-off-by: KanuaK <yihan_z@qq.com>

* [TritonToLinalg](perf) reuse true buffers for constant tail selects

Recognize tail masks whose selected interval reaches the tensor extent. For a constant false value and single-use true value, insert the false prefix into the true tensor so bufferization can reuse the computed buffer.

Keep direct slices for other Ascend 950 selects and the existing dynamic bounds guard. Add lowering and device coverage for constant tails, shared true values, mixed kernels, and out-of-range bounds.

---------

Signed-off-by: KanuaK <yihan_z@qq.com>
(cherry picked from commit 122e39178877cd4eca7536728221cfa84e661bac)

new file mode 100644
@@ -0,0 +1,348 @@
+// RUN: triton-opt --triton-to-linalg="compile-on-910-95=false" --split-input-file --verify-each %s | FileCheck %s --check-prefixes=COMMON,A2 --enable-var-scope
+// RUN: triton-opt --triton-to-linalg="compile-on-910-95=true" --split-input-file --verify-each %s | FileCheck %s --check-prefixes=COMMON,A5 --enable-var-scope
+
+// A pure-vector runtime point retains the guard on both targets. On 950,
+// only the selected element is copied; A2/A3 keep every slice start at zero.
+module {
+  func.func @dynamic_point(%true: tensor<16xi32>, %false: tensor<16xi32>, %position: i32) -> tensor<16xi32> {
+    %range = tt.make_range {start = 0 : i32, end = 16 : i32} : tensor<16xi32>
+    %positions = tt.splat %position : i32 -> tensor<16xi32>
+    %mask = arith.cmpi eq, %range, %positions : tensor<16xi32>
+    %result = arith.select %mask, %true, %false : tensor<16xi1>, tensor<16xi32>
+    return %result : tensor<16xi32>
+  }
+}
+// COMMON-LABEL: func.func @dynamic_point(
+// COMMON-SAME: %[[T:[^ :]+]]: tensor<16xi32>, %[[F:[^ :]+]]: tensor<16xi32>, %[[P:[^ :]+]]: i32
+// COMMON-DAG: %[[ZERO:.*]] = arith.constant 0 : index
+// COMMON-DAG: %[[N:.*]] = arith.constant 16 : index
+// COMMON: %[[POS:.*]] = arith.index_cast %[[P]] : i32 to index
+// COMMON-NOT: tensor.extract_slice
+// COMMON-NOT: tensor.insert_slice
+// COMMON: %[[NEG:.*]] = arith.cmpi slt, %[[POS]], %[[ZERO]]
+// COMMON: %[[PAST:.*]] = arith.cmpi sge, %[[POS]], %[[N]]
+// COMMON: %[[OOB:.*]] = arith.ori %[[NEG]], %[[PAST]]
+// COMMON: %[[RESULT:.*]] = scf.if %[[OOB]] -> (tensor<16xi32>) {
+// COMMON-NEXT: scf.yield %[[F]] : tensor<16xi32>
+// COMMON-NEXT: } else {
+// A5-NEXT: %[[PART:.*]] = tensor.extract_slice %[[T]][%[[POS]]] [1] [1]
+// A5-NEXT: %[[INSERT:.*]] = tensor.insert_slice %[[PART]] into %[[F]][%[[POS]]] [1] [1]
+// A2-NEXT: %[[PREFIX:.*]] = tensor.extract_slice %[[F]][0] [%[[POS]]] [1]
+// A2-NEXT: %[[TMP:.*]] = tensor.insert_slice %[[PREFIX]] into %[[T]][0] [%[[POS]]] [1]
+// A2-NEXT: %[[PART:.*]] = tensor.extract_slice %[[TMP]][0] [%[[END:.*]]] [1]
+// A2-NEXT: %[[INSERT:.*]] = tensor.insert_slice %[[PART]] into %[[F]][0] [%[[END]]] [1]
+// COMMON-NEXT: scf.yield %[[INSERT]] : tensor<16xi32>
+// COMMON-NEXT: }
+// COMMON-NEXT: return %[[RESULT]] : tensor<16xi32>
+
+// -----
+
+module {
+  func.func @dynamic_window(%true: tensor<16xf32>, %false: tensor<16xf32>, %lo: i32, %hi: i32) -> tensor<16xf32> {
+    %range = tt.make_range {start = 0 : i32, end = 16 : i32} : tensor<16xi32>
+    %los = tt.splat %lo : i32 -> tensor<16xi32>
+    %his = tt.splat %hi : i32 -> tensor<16xi32>
+    %lower = arith.cmpi sge, %range, %los : tensor<16xi32>
+    %upper = arith.cmpi slt, %range, %his : tensor<16xi32>
+    %mask = arith.andi %lower, %upper : tensor<16xi1>
+    %result = arith.select %mask, %true, %false : tensor<16xi1>, tensor<16xf32>
+    return %result : tensor<16xf32>
+  }
+}
+// COMMON-LABEL: func.func @dynamic_window(
+// COMMON-SAME: %[[T:[^ :]+]]: tensor<16xf32>, %[[F:[^ :]+]]: tensor<16xf32>
+// COMMON-NOT: tensor.extract_slice
+// COMMON-NOT: tensor.insert_slice
+// COMMON: scf.if

+import pytest

+import triton
+import triton.language as tl

+@triton.jit
+def _select_dynamic_offset_kernel(true_ptr, false_ptr, bounds_ptr, out_ptr, ROWS: tl.constexpr, COLS: tl.constexpr,
+                                  STEPS: tl.constexpr, MODE: tl.constexpr):
+    pid = tl.program_id(0)
+    cols = tl.arange(0, COLS)
+    offsets = tl.arange(0, ROWS)[:, None] * COLS + cols[None, :]
+    selected = tl.load(false_ptr + offsets)
+    for step in range(STEPS):
+        lo = tl.load(bounds_ptr + (pid * STEPS + step) * 2)
+        hi = tl.load(bounds_ptr + (pid * STEPS + step) * 2 + 1)
+        true_value = tl.load(true_ptr + step * ROWS * COLS + offsets)
+        if MODE == "head":
+            mask = cols < hi
+        elif MODE == "tail":
+            mask = cols >= lo
+        elif MODE == "point":
+            mask = cols == lo
+        else:
+            mask = (cols >= lo) & (cols < hi)
+        selected = tl.where(mask[None, :], true_value, selected)
+    tl.store(out_ptr + pid * ROWS * COLS + offsets, selected)
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32, torch.int32])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rows", [1, 8])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("mode", ["head", "tail", "middle", "point"])
+def test_select_dynamic_offset(dtype, rows, mode):
+    # Bounds are loaded from memory without alignment hints. Include starts
+    # around 32B boundaries, empty/disjoint intervals, and out-of-range points.
+    cols, steps = 64, 3
+    cases = torch.tensor([
+        [-3, 5],
+        [-1, 7],
+        [0, 0],
+        [1, 9],
+        [7, 15],
+        [8, 16],
+        [9, 17],
+        [63, 71],
+        [64, 72],
+        [67, 75],
+        [7, 7],
+        [9, 3],
+    ], dtype=torch.int32)
+    bounds = torch.stack([cases.roll(step, 0) for step in range(steps)], dim=1)
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(13)
+    true_value = torch.randint(-100, 100, (steps, rows, cols), generator=generator).to(dtype)
+    false_value = torch.randint(-100, 100, (rows, cols), generator=generator).to(dtype)
+    expected = false_value.expand(len(cases), rows, cols).clone()
+    offsets = torch.arange(cols)
+    for case in range(len(cases)):
+        for step in range(steps):
+            lo, hi = bounds[case, step]
+            if mode == "head":
+                mask = offsets < hi
+            elif mode == "tail":
+                mask = offsets >= lo
+            elif mode == "point":
+                mask = offsets == lo
+            else:
+                mask = (offsets >= lo) & (offsets < hi)
+            expected[case] = torch.where(mask[None, :], true_value[step], expected[case])

+    output = torch.empty(expected.shape, dtype=dtype, device="npu")
+    _select_dynamic_offset_kernel[(len(cases), )](
+        true_value.npu(),
+        false_value.npu(),
+        bounds.npu(),

+        STEPS=steps,
+        MODE=mode,
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(output.cpu(), expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _select_constant_tail_kernel(true_ptr, bounds_ptr, out_ptr, ROWS: tl.constexpr, COLS: tl.constexpr,
+                                 STEPS: tl.constexpr, AXIS: tl.constexpr, FALSE_VALUE: tl.constexpr):
+    pid = tl.program_id(0)
+    rows = tl.arange(0, ROWS)
+    cols = tl.arange(0, COLS)
+    offsets = rows[:, None] * COLS + cols[None, :]
+    for step in range(STEPS):
+        start = tl.load(bounds_ptr + pid * STEPS + step)
+        value = tl.load(true_ptr + step * ROWS * COLS + offsets) + step
+        if AXIS == 0:
+            mask = rows[:, None] >= start
+        else:
+            mask = cols[None, :] >= start
+        selected = tl.where(mask, value, FALSE_VALUE)
+        tl.store(out_ptr + (pid * STEPS + step) * ROWS * COLS + offsets, selected)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float32, torch.int32])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("axis", [0, 1])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("false_value", [0, -7])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("multibuffer", [False, True])
+def test_select_constant_tail(dtype, axis, false_value, multibuffer):
+    # Match KDA's outer-axis tail and shared loop-invariant constant, including
+    # starts around the sub-block split and outside the tensor. Also cover the
+    # last axis so the destination choice is independent of the mask axis.
+    rows, cols, steps = 32, 128, 3
+    extent = (rows, cols)[axis]
+    cases = torch.tensor([-3, -1, 0, 1, 7, 8, 9, 15, 16, 17, extent - 1, extent, extent + 3], dtype=torch.int32)
+    bounds = torch.stack([cases.roll(step, 0) for step in range(steps)], dim=1)
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(13)
+    true_value = torch.randint(-100, 100, (steps, rows, cols), generator=generator).to(dtype)
+    expected = torch.empty((len(cases), steps, rows, cols), dtype=dtype)
+    offsets = torch.arange(extent)
+    for case in range(len(cases)):
+        for step in range(steps):
+            mask = offsets >= bounds[case, step]
+            mask = mask[:, None] if axis == 0 else mask[None, :]
+            expected[case, step] = torch.where(mask, true_value[step] + step, false_value)
+
+    output = torch.empty(expected.shape, dtype=dtype, device="npu")
+    _select_constant_tail_kernel[(len(cases), )](
+        true_value.npu(),
+        bounds.npu(),
+        output,
+        ROWS=rows,
+        COLS=cols,
+        STEPS=steps,
+        AXIS=axis,
+        FALSE_VALUE=false_value,
+        multibuffer=multibuffer,
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(output.cpu(), expected, rtol=0, atol=0)

@@ -0,0 +1,36 @@
+// RUN: triton-opt '--triton-to-structured=compile-on-910-95=true' --verify-each %s | FileCheck %s
+
+// Reduced address pattern from the bucket-softmax regression:
+//   base + y + 8 * bucket, with result shape [8, 1, 2048].
+// The loaded indices stand in for the data-dependent bucket calculation.
+// Permuting to [2048, 8, 1] gives only 8 * sizeof(f32) = 32 contiguous
+// bytes. Keep the original load shape and do not insert tt.trans.
+// CHECK-LABEL: tt.func public @skip_short_contiguous_load(
+// CHECK-NOT: ImplicitPermuteHandled
+// CHECK-NOT: tt.trans
+// CHECK: %[[LOAD:.*]] = tt.load {{.*}} : tensor<8x1x2048x!tt.ptr<f32>>
+// CHECK-NOT: ImplicitPermuteHandled
+// CHECK-NOT: tt.trans
+// CHECK: tt.return %[[LOAD]] : tensor<8x1x2048xf32>
+module {
+  tt.func public @skip_short_contiguous_load(%base: !tt.ptr<f32>, %indices: !tt.ptr<i32>) -> tensor<8x1x2048xf32> {
+    %irange = tt.make_range {start = 0 : i32, end = 2048 : i32} : tensor<2048xi32>
+    %ibase = tt.splat %indices : !tt.ptr<i32> -> tensor<2048x!tt.ptr<i32>>
+    %iptr = tt.addptr %ibase, %irange : tensor<2048x!tt.ptr<i32>>, tensor<2048xi32>
+    %token = tt.load %iptr : tensor<2048x!tt.ptr<i32>>
+    %token_2d = tt.expand_dims %token {axis = 0 : i32} : tensor<2048xi32> -> tensor<1x2048xi32>
+    %data = tt.expand_dims %token_2d {axis = 0 : i32} : tensor<1x2048xi32> -> tensor<1x1x2048xi32>
+    %scale = arith.constant dense<8> : tensor<1x1x2048xi32>
+    %scaled = arith.muli %data, %scale : tensor<1x1x2048xi32>
+    %cols = tt.broadcast %scaled : tensor<1x1x2048xi32> -> tensor<8x1x2048xi32>
+    %y = tt.make_range {start = 0 : i32, end = 8 : i32} : tensor<8xi32>
+    %y_2d = tt.expand_dims %y {axis = 1 : i32} : tensor<8xi32> -> tensor<8x1xi32>
+    %y_3d = tt.expand_dims %y_2d {axis = 2 : i32} : tensor<8x1xi32> -> tensor<8x1x1xi32>
+    %rows = tt.broadcast %y_3d : tensor<8x1x1xi32> -> tensor<8x1x2048xi32>
+    %offset = arith.addi %rows, %cols : tensor<8x1x2048xi32>
+    %base_tile = tt.splat %base : !tt.ptr<f32> -> tensor<8x1x2048x!tt.ptr<f32>>
+    %ptr = tt.addptr %base_tile, %offset : tensor<8x1x2048x!tt.ptr<f32>>, tensor<8x1x2048xi32>
+    %value = tt.load %ptr : tensor<8x1x2048x!tt.ptr<f32>>
+    tt.return %value : tensor<8x1x2048xf32>
+  }
+}

[language](fix) 以 patch 方式修复 Python 3.14 aggregate 哈希包含 __annotate__ (#3045)

Python 3.14 按 PEP 649 为带注解的类合成 __annotate__，_aggregate 通过
inspect.getmembers 收集成员时会把它写入 hash_attrs，导致
runtime/jit.py::record_reference 抛出 "Unsupported function referenced"，
test_aggregate_with_tuple 因此失败。

按 Ascend 仓约定，不直接修改社区文件 python/triton/language/core.py，
而是把改动写入 third_party/ascend/patch/triton-ascend-3.6.0.patch，
并将 core.py 加入 setup_patch.py 的 patch 白名单。

代码与注释对齐上游最新实现（#9529 与 #10581）：__annotate__ 与
__annotate_func__ 均跳过，不额外发挥。

(cherry picked from commit 9e74ed81e2850377f814d162e1fd332f65ecc74c)

+// RUN: triton-opt %s -graph-optimize='compile-on-910-95=false' --verify-each | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=OTHER

+
+// Reuse a shared wide producer instead of duplicating its XOR at i32.
+// CHECK-LABEL: tt.func @shared_wide_xor(
+// CHECK: %[[SHARED:.*]] = arith.xori {{.*}} : tensor<128xi64>
+// CHECK-NOT: arith.xori
+// CHECK: %[[LOW:.*]] = arith.trunci %[[SHARED]] : tensor<128xi64> to tensor<128xi32>
+// CHECK-NOT: arith.xori
+// CHECK: arith.andi %[[LOW]], {{.*}} : tensor<128xi32>
+// CHECK-NOT: arith.xori
+// CHECK: tt.return %[[SHARED]],
+// OTHER-LABEL: tt.func @shared_wide_xor(
+// OTHER: arith.xori {{.*}} : tensor<128xi64>
+// OTHER: arith.andi {{.*}} : tensor<128xi64>
+tt.func @shared_wide_xor(%a: tensor<128xi64>, %b: tensor<128xi64>) -> (tensor<128xi64>, tensor<128xi64>) {
+  %mask = arith.constant dense<255> : tensor<128xi64>
+  %shared = arith.xori %a, %b : tensor<128xi64>
+  %masked = arith.andi %shared, %mask : tensor<128xi64>
+  tt.return %shared, %masked : tensor<128xi64>, tensor<128xi64>
+}
+
+// Recurse through the private XOR, then stop at its shared upstream producer.
+// CHECK-LABEL: tt.func @deep_shared_xor(
+// CHECK: %[[DEEP_SHARED:.*]] = arith.xori {{.*}} : tensor<128xi64>
+// CHECK-NOT: arith.xori
+// CHECK: %[[LOW_SHARED:.*]] = arith.trunci %[[DEEP_SHARED]] : tensor<128xi64> to tensor<128xi32>
+// CHECK: %[[LOW_C:.*]] = arith.trunci {{.*}} : tensor<128xi64> to tensor<128xi32>
+// CHECK: %[[PRIVATE:.*]] = arith.xori %[[LOW_SHARED]], %[[LOW_C]] : tensor<128xi32>
+// CHECK-NOT: arith.xori
+// CHECK: arith.andi %[[PRIVATE]], {{.*}} : tensor<128xi32>
+// CHECK-NOT: arith.xori
+// CHECK: tt.return %[[DEEP_SHARED]],
+// OTHER-LABEL: tt.func @deep_shared_xor(

+// OTHER: arith.andi {{.*}} : tensor<128xi64>
+tt.func @deep_shared_xor(%a: tensor<128xi64>, %b: tensor<128xi64>, %c: tensor<128xi64>) -> (tensor<128xi64>, tensor<128xi64>) {
+  %mask = arith.constant dense<255> : tensor<128xi64>
+  %shared = arith.xori %a, %b : tensor<128xi64>
+  %private = arith.xori %shared, %c : tensor<128xi64>
+  %masked = arith.andi %private, %mask : tensor<128xi64>
+  tt.return %shared, %masked : tensor<128xi64>, tensor<128xi64>
+}

+// The replacement root itself may have multiple uses. Truncating it instead
+// would create a cycle when its uses are replaced with the new extension.
+// CHECK-LABEL: tt.func @multi_use_root(
+// CHECK-NOT: arith.andi {{.*}} : tensor<128xi64>
+// CHECK: %[[ROOT:.*]] = arith.andi {{.*}} : tensor<128xi32>
+// CHECK: %[[EXTENDED_ROOT:.*]] = arith.extui %[[ROOT]] : tensor<128xi32> to tensor<128xi64>
+// CHECK: tt.return %[[EXTENDED_ROOT]], %[[EXTENDED_ROOT]]
+// OTHER-LABEL: tt.func @multi_use_root(

+// OTHER: tt.return %[[WIDE_ROOT]], %[[WIDE_ROOT]]

+  %mask = arith.constant dense<255> : tensor<128xi64>
+  %masked = arith.andi %a, %mask : tensor<128xi64>
+  tt.return %masked, %masked : tensor<128xi64>, tensor<128xi64>
+}
+
+// Keep narrowing useful when the original wide producer can be removed.
+// CHECK-LABEL: tt.func @private_xor(
+// CHECK-NOT: arith.xori {{.*}} : tensor<128xi64>
+// CHECK: %[[PRIVATE_LOW:.*]] = arith.xori {{.*}} : tensor<128xi32>
+// CHECK-NOT: arith.xori {{.*}} : tensor<128xi64>
+// CHECK: arith.andi %[[PRIVATE_LOW]], {{.*}} : tensor<128xi32>
+// CHECK-NOT: arith.xori {{.*}} : tensor<128xi64>
+// CHECK: tt.return

+  %private = arith.xori %a, %b : tensor<128xi64>

+// shared comparison RHS while preserving the scalar upper-bit guard.
+// CHECK-LABEL: tt.func @shared_comparison_inputs(
+// CHECK: %[[LIMIT:.*]] = tt.splat {{.*}} : i64 -> tensor<128xi64>

+// RUN: triton-opt %s -graph-optimize='compile-on-910-95=false' --verify-each | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=OTHER
+//
+// Reduced from one byte-selection round of _radix_topk_threshold, BLOCK_R=8192.
+// Preserve its u32 key extraction, zero parking and bin-zero correction.
+// All four radix rounds use this structure. This is not an end-to-end kernel.
+//
+// CHECK-LABEL: tt.func @radix_topk_threshold_round(
+// CHECK-NOT: tt.reduce
+// CHECK-NOT: arith.subi
+// CHECK-NOT: tt.histogram
+// CHECK: arith.shrui {{.*}} : tensor<8192xi32>
+// CHECK-NOT: tt.reduce
+// CHECK-NOT: arith.subi
+// CHECK-NOT: tt.histogram
+// CHECK: arith.constant dense<-1> : tensor<8192xi32>
+// CHECK: tt.histogram
+// CHECK-NOT: tt.histogram
+// CHECK-NOT: tt.reduce
+// CHECK-NOT: arith.subi
+// CHECK: tt.return
+// OTHER-LABEL: tt.func @radix_topk_threshold_round(
+// OTHER: arith.shrui {{.*}} : tensor<8192xi64>
+// OTHER: tt.histogram
+// OTHER: tt.reduce
+// OTHER: arith.subi
+tt.func @radix_topk_threshold_round(%keys: tensor<8192xi64>, %live: tensor<8192xi1>) -> tensor<256xi32> {
+  %u32mask = arith.constant dense<4294967295> : tensor<8192xi64>
+  %shift = arith.constant dense<24> : tensor<8192xi64>
+  %byte_mask = arith.constant dense<255> : tensor<8192xi64>
+  %zero = arith.constant dense<0> : tensor<8192xi32>
+  %true = arith.constant dense<true> : tensor<8192xi1>
+  %zero_bins = arith.constant dense<0> : tensor<256xi32>
+  %bounded = arith.andi %keys, %u32mask : tensor<8192xi64>
+  %shifted = arith.shrui %bounded, %shift : tensor<8192xi64>
+  %byte = arith.andi %shifted, %byte_mask : tensor<8192xi64>
+  %indices = arith.trunci %byte : tensor<8192xi64> to tensor<8192xi32>
+  %parked = arith.select %live, %indices, %zero : tensor<8192xi1>, tensor<8192xi32>
+  %hist = tt.histogram %parked : tensor<8192xi32> -> tensor<256xi32>
+  %invalid = arith.xori %live, %true : tensor<8192xi1>
+  %counts = arith.extui %invalid : tensor<8192xi1> to tensor<8192xi32>
+  %count = "tt.reduce"(%counts) ({
+  ^bb0(%a: i32, %b: i32):
+    %sum = arith.addi %a, %b : i32
+    tt.reduce.return %sum : i32
+  }) {axis = 0 : i32} : (tensor<8192xi32>) -> i32
+  %splat = tt.splat %count : i32 -> tensor<256xi32>
+  %bins = tt.make_range {start = 0 : i32, end = 256 : i32} : tensor<256xi32>
+  %iszero = arith.cmpi eq, %bins, %zero_bins : tensor<256xi32>
+  %correction = arith.select %iszero, %splat, %zero_bins : tensor<256xi1>, tensor<256xi32>
+  %result = arith.subi %hist, %correction : tensor<256xi32>
+  tt.return %result : tensor<256xi32>
+}

+# Copyright (c) Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. 2026. All rights reserved.
+"""Fold parked bin-zero counts without losing genuine zeros or other users."""
+import pytest
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+from triton.backends.ascend.utils import is_compile_on_910_95
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _parking(X, M, O, N: tl.constexpr, BINS: tl.constexpr, PARK: tl.constexpr, WRONG_MASK: tl.constexpr,
+             KEEP_RAW: tl.constexpr):
+    i = tl.arange(0, N)
+    mask = tl.load(M + i) != 0
+    x = tl.load(X + i)
+    hist = tl.histogram(tl.where(mask, x, PARK), BINS)
+    counted_mask = mask if not WRONG_MASK else (i % 3 == 0)
+    count = tl.sum((~counted_mask).to(tl.int32), 0)
+    bins = tl.arange(0, BINS)
+    corrected = hist - tl.where(bins == 0, count, 0)
+    tl.store(O + bins, corrected)
+    tl.store(O + BINS + bins, hist if KEEP_RAW else corrected)
+
+
+def _check_parking(size, bins, park, wrong_mask, mask_kind, keep_raw=False):
+    torch.manual_seed(37)
+    x = torch.randint(-8, bins + 8, (size, ), dtype=torch.int32)
+    x[::7] = 0
+    mask = torch.randint(0, 2, (size, ), dtype=torch.int32)
+    if mask_kind != "random":
+        mask.fill_(int(mask_kind == "all"))
+    device_x, device_mask = x.npu(), mask.npu()
+    output = torch.empty((2, bins), dtype=torch.int32, device=device_x.device)
+    _parking[(1, )](device_x, device_mask, output, size, bins, park, wrong_mask, keep_raw, enable_graph_optimize=True)
+    parked = torch.where(mask.bool(), x, park)
+    hist = torch.bincount(parked[(parked >= 0) & (parked < bins)].long(), minlength=bins)
+    count_mask = torch.arange(size) % 3 == 0 if wrong_mask else mask.bool()
+    expected = hist.clone()
+    expected[0] -= (~count_mask).sum()
+    second = hist if keep_raw else expected
+    torch.testing.assert_close(output.cpu().long(), torch.stack((expected, second)), rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("size", [256, 8192])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("bins", [16, 256])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("park,wrong_mask", [(0, False), (1, False), (0, True)])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("mask_kind", ["random", "none", "all"])
+def test_histogram_parking(size, bins, park, wrong_mask, mask_kind):
+    # The N=8192 zero-parking shapes exercise the A5 histogram path. On A3,
+    # their baseline TTIR exceeds UB capacity before graph optimization can
+    # lower it, irrespective of whether the correction mask matches.
+    if not is_compile_on_910_95() and size == 8192 and park == 0:
+        pytest.skip("A5-only zero-parking histogram shape exceeds A3 UB")
+    _check_parking(size, bins, park, wrong_mask, mask_kind)
+
+
+def test_histogram_parking_other_users():
+    _check_parking(8192, 256, 0, False, "random", keep_raw=True)

+# Copyright (c) Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. 2026. All rights reserved.
+"""Unsigned narrowing must preserve upper-bit checks and signed shifts."""
+import pytest
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _narrow_bits(X, T, O, N: tl.constexpr, SHIFT: tl.constexpr):
+    i = tl.arange(0, N)
+    x = tl.load(X + i)
+    t = tl.load(T)
+    u = x & 0xffffffff
+    key = tl.where(x < 0, (~u) & 0xffffffff, u | 0x80000000)
+    tl.store(O + i, key >> SHIFT)
+    tl.store(O + N + i, (key >> SHIFT) == t)
+    # This shift must NOT be changed to unsigned, nor narrowed before shifting.
+    tl.store(O + 2 * N + i, x >> SHIFT)
+    tl.store(O + 3 * N + i, x)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("shift", [0, 8, 24, 31])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("threshold", [-1, 0, 255, 0x1000000ff])
+def test_unsigned_tensor_narrowing(shift, threshold):
+    values = torch.tensor([
+        -(1 << 63), -0x100000001, -1, 0, 1, 255, 0x7fffffff, 0x80000000, 0xffffffff, 0x100000000, 0x1000000ff,
+        (1 << 63) - 1, -255, 0x123456789abcdef, -0x123456789abcdef, 42
+    ], dtype=torch.int64, device="npu")
+    target = torch.tensor([threshold], dtype=torch.int64, device=values.device)
+    output = torch.empty((4, 16), dtype=torch.int64, device=values.device)
+    _narrow_bits[(1, )](values, target, output, 16, shift, enable_graph_optimize=True)
+    x = values.cpu()
